items.title: 68099_Erskine Hawkins oral history interview
items.q: I had another fellow there by the name of Bill Johnson, first alto. He came in later. He was arranger.

ctx.x: Well, it's beginning to appear more and more that you began to emerge as the band leader because you were the one who was able to do everything. I mean, that you were, you had a particular focus. Did you have a sound in mind for the band? I mean, did you have a specific way that you thought it should sound?

As the arrangements came in, we took it from there. More arrangements from Sam. I had another fellow there by the name of Bill Johnson, first alto. He came in later. He was arranger. William McLamore, he came in later. And then we, after that, after I got all these arranged together, then I used to sit with them and we'd talk it over. And then, I'd use just a certain swing, certain tempo I wanted, I liked, in that swing tempo. Then, once we got into that, then the sound came a little later. They started Bill and…
doing the, you know, regular solos now that I was leading.
